chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال ابن إسحاق: ثم كانت غزوة الخندق في شوال سنة خمس. فحدثني يزيد بن رومان، عن عروة، ومن لا أتهم، عن عبد الله بن كعب بن مالك، ومحمد بن كعب القرظي، والزهري، وعاصم بن عمر بن قتادة، وعبد الله بن أبي بكر، وغيرهم من علمائنا، وبعضهم يحدث ما لا يحدث بعض.
قالوا: إنه كان من حديث الخندق أن نفرًا من اليهود – منهم سلام بن أبي الحقيق النضري، وحيي بن أخطب النضري، وكنانة بن الربيع بن أبي الحقيق، وهوذة بن قيس الوائلي، وأبو عمار الوائلي، في نفر من بني النضير ونفر من بني وائل، وهم الذين حزَّبوا الأحزاب على رسول الله ﷺ – خرجوا حتى قدموا على قريش بمكة.
فدعوهم إلى حرب رسول الله ﷺ، وقالوا: إنا سنكون معكم عليه حتى نستأصله. فقالت لهم قريش: يا معشر يهود، إنكم أهل الكتاب الأول والعلم بما أصبحنا نختلف فيه نحن ومحمد؛ أفديننا خير أم دينه؟ قالوا: بل دينكم خير من دينه، وأنتم أولى بالحق منه.
فهم الذين أنزل الله فيهم:
﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْجِبْتِ وَالطَّاغُوتِ وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَؤُلَاءِ أَهْدَىٰ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا سَبِيلًا ۝ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَمَنْ يَلْعَنِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ نَصِيرًا﴾ [النساء: ٥١–٥٢].
فلما قالوا ذلك لقريش سُرُّوا ونشطوا لما دعوهم إليه من حرب رسول الله ﷺ، فاجتمعوا لذلك واتعدوا له.
ثم خرج أولئك النفر من يهود حتى جاءوا غطفان من قيس عيلان، فدعوهم إلى حرب النبي ﷺ، وأخبروهم أنهم سيكونون معهم عليه، وأن قريشًا قد تابعوهم على ذلك واجتمعوا معهم فيه.
فخرجت قريش وقائدها أبو سفيان، وخرجت غطفان وقائدها عيينة بن حصن بن حذيفة بن بدر، في بني فزارة، والحارث بن عوف بن أبي حارثة المري، في بني مرة، ومسعر بن رخيلة بن نويرة بن طريف بن سحمة بن عبد الله بن هلال بن خلاوة بن أشجع بن ريث بن غطفان، فيمن تابعه من قومه من أشجع.
فلما سمع بهم رسول الله ﷺ وما أجمعوا له من الأمر، ضرب الخندق على المدينة.
سيرة ابن إسحاق (٢/٢١٤–٢١٥).
قال ابن هشام (٢/٢٢٤): يقال إن سلمان الفارسي أشار به على رسول الله ﷺ، يعني حفر الخندق.

Ibn Isḥāq said: The Campaign of the Trench then took place in Shawwāl of the fifth year. Yazīd ibn Rūmān related to me from ʿUrwah, while other trustworthy narrators related from ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, al-Zuhrī, ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah, ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, and other scholars. Some of them related details that others did not.
They said: The account of the Trench began when a group of Jews—including Sallām ibn Abī al-Ḥuqayq al-Naḍarī, Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab al-Naḍarī, Kinānah ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Abī al-Ḥuqayq, Hawdhah ibn Qays al-Wāʾilī, and Abū ʿAmmār al-Wāʾilī, together with men of Banū al-Naḍīr and Banū Wāʾil—set out for Quraysh in Makkah. They were the ones who assembled the confederate forces against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They called Quraysh to wage war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, “We shall stand with you against him until we eradicate him.” Quraysh asked them, “Jews, you are the people of the earlier scripture and possess knowledge of the matter over which Muhammad and we disagree. Is our religion better or his?” They replied, “Your religion is better than his, and you have a greater claim to the truth.”
It was concerning them that Allah revealed:
“Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in false gods and idols, and say of the disbelievers, ‘These are better guided than the believers.’ Those are the ones Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses, you will never find any helper for him.”
 [Al-Nisāʾ 4:51–52]
When they said this to Quraysh, Quraysh were delighted and became enthusiastic about their call to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They gathered and made preparations for it.
Those Jewish representatives then went to Ghaṭafān of Qays ʿAylān and called them to fight the Prophet ﷺ. They informed them that they would stand alongside them against him and that Quraysh had already agreed to participate and join forces with them.
Quraysh marched under the leadership of Abū Sufyān. Ghaṭafān also marched: ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfah ibn Badr led Banū Fazārah; al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf ibn Abī Ḥārithah al-Murrī led Banū Murrah; and Misʿar ibn Rukhaylah ibn Nuwayrah ibn Ṭarīf ibn Saḥmah ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Hilāl ibn Khalāwah ibn Ashjaʿ ibn Rayth ibn Ghaṭafān led those of Ashjaʿ who followed him.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ learned of their advance and what they had united to do against him, he had the trench dug around Madinah.
The Sīrah of Ibn Isḥāq (2/214–215).
Ibn Hishām said (2/224): It is related that Salmān al-Fārisī suggested this strategy to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—that is, digging the trench.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى حاكيًا عن عيسى بن مريم:
 (وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ: يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ، إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللهِ إِلَيْكُم، مُّصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ، وَمُبَشِّرًا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُم بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالُوا: هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ) [الصف: ٦].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا، قُلْ: كَفَىٰ بِاللهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ، وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ) [الرعد: ٤٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (كَذَٰلِكَ يُوحِي إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ اللهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) [الشورى: ٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ، وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ، وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ، وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُورًا) [النساء: ١٦٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ، يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ) [البقرة: ١٤٦].
 وللبشارات الواردة في التوراة والإنجيل وكتب الهندوس، يراجع كتابي “دراسات في اليهودية والمسيحية وأديان الهند”.
chapters.intro_ar_display:
قال الله تعالى حاكيًا عن عيسى بن مريم:
 (وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ: يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ، إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللهِ إِلَيْكُم، مُّصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ، وَمُبَشِّرًا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ، فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُم بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالُوا: هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ) [الصف: ٦].
وقال تعالى:
 (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا، قُلْ: كَفَىٰ بِاللهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ، وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ) [الرعد: ٤٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (كَذَٰلِكَ يُوحِي إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ اللهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) [الشورى: ٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ، وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ، وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ، وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُورًا) [النساء: ١٦٣].
وقال تعالى:
 (الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ، يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ) [البقرة: ١٤٦].
 وللبشارات الواردة في التوراة والإنجيل وكتب الهندوس، يراجع كتابي “دراسات في اليهودية والمسيحية وأديان الهند”.
chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High said, narrating from ‘Isa ibn Maryam:
 “And when ‘Isa ibn Maryam said: O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and giving glad tidings of a messenger to come after me whose name is Ahmad. But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said: This is clear magic.” [al-Ṣaff: 6]
And Allah Most High said:
 “Those who disbelieve say: You are not sent. Say: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.” [al-Ra‘d: 43]
And Allah Most High said:
 “Thus Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, reveals to you and to those before you.” [al-Shūrā: 3]
And Allah Most High said:
 “Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nūḥ and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Ibrahim, Isma‘il, Isḥaq, Ya‘qub, the Tribes, ‘Isa, Ayyub, Yunus, Harun, and Sulayman, and We gave Dawud the Zabur.” [al-Nisā’: 163]
And Allah Most High said:
 “Those to whom We gave the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons.” [al-Baqarah: 146]
 For the glad tidings found in the Torah, Gospel, and Hindu scriptures, refer to my book Studies in Judaism, Christianity, and the Religions of India.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال ابن إسحاق: ثم بعث رسول الله ﷺ خالد بن الوليد، في شهر ربيع الآخر أو جمادى الأولى سنة عشر، إلى بني الحارث بن كعب بنجران.
وأمره أن يدعوهم إلى الإسلام قبل أن يقاتلهم ثلاثًا؛ فإن استجابوا فاقبل منهم، وإن لم يفعلوا فقاتلهم.
فخرج خالد حتى قدم عليهم، فبعث الركبان يضربون في كل وجه، ويدعون إلى الإسلام، ويقولون: أيها الناس، أسلموا تسلموا.
فأسلم الناس ودخلوا فيما دعوا إليه.
فأقام فيهم خالد يعلمهم الإسلام وكتاب الله وسنة نبيه ﷺ، وبذلك كان أمره رسول الله ﷺ إن هم أسلموا ولم يقاتلوا.
ثم كتب خالد بن الوليد إلى رسول الله ﷺ:
من خالد بن الوليد، إلى محمد النبي رسول الله. السلام عليك يا رسول الله ورحمة الله وبركاته، فإني أحمد إليك الله الذي لا إله إلا هو.
أما بعد: يا رسول الله، صلى الله عليك، فإنك بعثتني إلى بني الحارث بن كعب، وأمرتني إذا أتيتهم ألا أقاتلهم ثلاثة أيام، وأن أدعوهم إلى الإسلام، فإن أسلموا أقمت فيهم، وقبلت منهم، وعلمتهم معالم الإسلام وكتاب الله وسنة نبيه، وإن لم يسلموا قاتلتهم.
وإني قدمت عليهم، فدعوتهم إلى الإسلام ثلاثة أيام كما أمرني رسول الله ﷺ، وبعثت فيهم ركبانًا قالوا: يا بني الحارث، أسلموا تسلموا.
فأسلموا ولم يقاتلوا، وأنا مقيم بين أظهرهم، آمرهم بما أمرهم الله به، وأنهاهم عما نهاهم الله عنه، وأعلمهم معالم الإسلام وسنة النبي ﷺ، حتى يكتب إليَّ رسول الله ﷺ.
والسلام عليك يا رسول الله ورحمة الله وبركاته.
فكتب إليه رسول الله ﷺ:
«بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. من محمد النبي رسول الله إلى خالد بن الوليد. سلام عليك، فإني أحمد إليك الله الذي لا إله إلا هو.
أما بعد: فإن كتابك جاءني مع رسولك، تخبر أن بني الحارث بن كعب قد أسلموا قبل أن تقاتلهم، وأجابوا إلى ما دعوتهم إليه من الإسلام، وشهدوا أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدًا عبد الله ورسوله، وأن قد هداهم الله بهداه.
فبشرهم وأنذرهم، وأقبل، وليقبل معك وفدهم. والسلام عليك ورحمة الله وبركاته».
فأقبل خالد إلى رسول الله ﷺ، وأقبل معه وفد بني الحارث بن كعب، منهم: قيس بن الحصين ذي الغصة، ويزيد بن عبد المدان، ويزيد بن المحجل، وعبد الله بن قراد الزيادي، وشداد بن عبد الله القناني، وعمرو بن عبد الله الضبابي.
فلما قدموا على رسول الله ﷺ فرآهم قال: «من هؤلاء القوم الذين كأنهم رجال الهند؟»
قيل: يا رسول الله، هؤلاء رجال بني الحارث بن كعب.
فلما وقفوا على رسول الله ﷺ سلموا عليه وقالوا: نشهد أنك رسول الله، وأنه لا إله إلا الله.
قال رسول الله ﷺ: «وأنا أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأني رسول الله».
ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أنتم الذين إذا زجروا استقدموا؟»
فسكتوا، فلم يراجعه منهم أحد.
ثم أعادها الثانية، فلم يراجعه منهم أحد. ثم أعادها الثالثة، فلم يراجعه منهم أحد.
ثم أعادها الرابعة، فقال يزيد بن عبد المدان: نعم يا رسول الله، نحن الذين إذا زجروا استقدموا. قالها أربع مرار.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «لو أن خالدًا لم يكتب إليَّ أنكم أسلمتم ولم تقاتلوا، لألقيت رؤوسكم تحت أقدامكم».
فقال يزيد بن عبد المدان: أما والله ما حمدناك ولا حمدنا خالدًا.
قال: «فمن حمدتم؟»
قالوا: حمدنا الله عز وجل الذي هدانا بك يا رسول الله.
قال: «صدقتم».
ثم قال رسول الله ﷺ: «بم كنتم تغلبون من قاتلكم في الجاهلية؟»
قالوا: لم نكن نغلب أحدًا.
قال: «بلى، قد كنتم تغلبون من قاتلكم».
قالوا: كنا نغلب من قاتلنا يا رسول الله؛ إنا كنا نجتمع ولا نفترق، ولا نبدأ أحدًا بظلم.
قال: «صدقتم».
وأمر رسول الله ﷺ على بني الحارث بن كعب قيس بن الحصين.
فرجع وفد بني الحارث إلى قومهم في بقية من شوال أو في صدر ذي القعدة.
فلم يمكثوا بعد أن رجعوا إلى قومهم إلا أربعة أشهر حتى توفي رسول الله ﷺ، ورحم وبارك ورضي وأنعم.
السيرة لابن هشام (٥٩٢–٥٩٤/٢)، وذكره البيهقي في الدلائل (٤١١–٤١٢/٥) بإسناده عن ابن إسحاق.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Ibn Isḥāq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd during Rabīʿ al-Ākhir or Jumādā al-Ūlā in the tenth year to Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb in Najrān.
He instructed him to invite them to Islam for three days before fighting them. If they responded, he was to accept their response; otherwise, he was to fight them.
Khālid traveled until he reached them. He sent riders in every direction to invite them to Islam, proclaiming, “O people, embrace Islam and you will be safe.”
The people embraced Islam and accepted what they were invited to.
Khālid remained among them, teaching them Islam, the Book of Allah, and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. This was what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had instructed him to do if they accepted Islam without fighting.
Khālid ibn al-Walīd then wrote to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“From Khālid ibn al-Walīd to Muḥammad, the Prophet and Messenger of Allah. Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. I praise Allah before you, besides whom there is no deity.
“To proceed: O Messenger of Allah, may Allah’s blessings be upon you. You sent me to Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb and instructed me not to fight them for three days after reaching them, but to invite them to Islam. If they embraced Islam, I was to remain among them, accept their profession of Islam, and teach them the principles of Islam, the Book of Allah, and the Sunnah of His Prophet. If they did not embrace Islam, I was to fight them.
“I reached them and invited them to Islam for three days, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed me. I sent riders among them proclaiming, ‘O Banū al-Ḥārith, embrace Islam and you will be safe.’
“They embraced Islam without fighting. I am now residing among them, commanding them to observe what Allah has commanded, forbidding them from what Allah has prohibited, and teaching them the principles of Islam and the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ writes further instructions to me.
“Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote back to him:
“In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muḥammad, the Prophet and Messenger of Allah, to Khālid ibn al-Walīd. Peace be upon you. I praise Allah before you, besides whom there is no deity.
“To proceed: Your letter has reached me with your messenger, informing me that Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb embraced Islam before you fought them; that they responded to your invitation to Islam; that they testified that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the servant and Messenger of Allah; and that Allah guided them through His guidance.
“Give them glad tidings and warn them. Then return, and let a delegation from them return with you. Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you.”
Khālid returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, accompanied by a delegation from Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb. Among them were Qays ibn al-Ḥuṣayn Dhū al-Ghuṣṣah, Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Madān, Yazīd ibn al-Muḥajjal, ʿAbdullāh ibn Qurād al-Ziyādī, Shaddād ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Qanānī, and ʿAmr ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Ḍubābī.
When they came before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he saw them, he asked: “Who are these men who look like men from India?”
He was told, “O Messenger of Allah, these are men from Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb.”
When they stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they greeted him and said, “We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah and that there is no deity except Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied: “And I testify that there is no deity except Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then asked: “Are you the people who advance when they are rebuked and driven back?”
They remained silent, and none of them answered him.
He repeated it a second time, but no one responded. He repeated it a third time, but still no one responded.
When he repeated it a fourth time, Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Madān said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are the people who advance when driven back.” He said this four times.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Had Khālid not written to me that you embraced Islam without fighting, I would have cast your heads beneath your feet.”
Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Madān replied, “By Allah, we did not praise you, nor did we praise Khālid.”
He asked: “Whom, then, did you praise?”
They replied, “We praised Allah Almighty, who guided us through you, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said: “You have spoken the truth.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then asked: “Through what qualities did you defeat those who fought you during the pre-Islamic period?”
They replied, “We did not defeat anyone.”
He said: “Indeed, you did defeat those who fought you.”
They replied, “We defeated those who fought us, O Messenger of Allah, because we remained united and did not divide, and we never initiated injustice against anyone.”
He said: “You have spoken the truth.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Qays ibn al-Ḥuṣayn as leader over Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb.
The delegation of Banū al-Ḥārith returned to their people during the remaining days of Shawwāl or at the beginning of Dhū al-Qaʿdah.
Only four months passed after their return before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died—may Allah bestow mercy, blessings, pleasure, and favor upon him.

chapters.intro_en_display:
Ibn Isḥāq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd during Rabīʿ al-Ākhir or Jumādā al-Ūlā in the tenth year to Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb in Najrān.
He instructed him to invite them to Islam for three days before fighting them. If they responded, he was to accept their response; otherwise, he was to fight them.
Khālid traveled until he reached them. He sent riders in every direction to invite them to Islam, proclaiming, “O people, embrace Islam and you will be safe.”
The people embraced Islam and accepted what they were invited to.
Khālid remained among them, teaching them Islam, the Book of Allah, and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. This was what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had instructed him to do if they accepted Islam without fighting.
Khālid ibn al-Walīd then wrote to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
“From Khālid ibn al-Walīd to Muḥammad, the Prophet and Messenger of Allah. Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. I praise Allah before you, besides whom there is no deity.
“To proceed: O Messenger of Allah, may Allah’s blessings be upon you. You sent me to Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb and instructed me not to fight them for three days after reaching them, but to invite them to Islam. If they embraced Islam, I was to remain among them, accept their profession of Islam, and teach them the principles of Islam, the Book of Allah, and the Sunnah of His Prophet. If they did not embrace Islam, I was to fight them.
“I reached them and invited them to Islam for three days, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed me. I sent riders among them proclaiming, ‘O Banū al-Ḥārith, embrace Islam and you will be safe.’
“They embraced Islam without fighting. I am now residing among them, commanding them to observe what Allah has commanded, forbidding them from what Allah has prohibited, and teaching them the principles of Islam and the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ writes further instructions to me.
“Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote back to him:
“In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muḥammad, the Prophet and Messenger of Allah, to Khālid ibn al-Walīd. Peace be upon you. I praise Allah before you, besides whom there is no deity.
“To proceed: Your letter has reached me with your messenger, informing me that Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb embraced Islam before you fought them; that they responded to your invitation to Islam; that they testified that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the servant and Messenger of Allah; and that Allah guided them through His guidance.
“Give them glad tidings and warn them. Then return, and let a delegation from them return with you. Peace, mercy, and blessings of Allah be upon you.”
Khālid returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, accompanied by a delegation from Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb. Among them were Qays ibn al-Ḥuṣayn Dhū al-Ghuṣṣah, Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Madān, Yazīd ibn al-Muḥajjal, ʿAbdullāh ibn Qurād al-Ziyādī, Shaddād ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Qanānī, and ʿAmr ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Ḍubābī.
When they came before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he saw them, he asked: “Who are these men who look like men from India?”
He was told, “O Messenger of Allah, these are men from Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb.”
When they stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they greeted him and said, “We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah and that there is no deity except Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied: “And I testify that there is no deity except Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then asked: “Are you the people who advance when they are rebuked and driven back?”
They remained silent, and none of them answered him.
He repeated it a second time, but no one responded. He repeated it a third time, but still no one responded.
When he repeated it a fourth time, Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Madān said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are the people who advance when driven back.” He said this four times.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Had Khālid not written to me that you embraced Islam without fighting, I would have cast your heads beneath your feet.”
Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Madān replied, “By Allah, we did not praise you, nor did we praise Khālid.”
He asked: “Whom, then, did you praise?”
They replied, “We praised Allah Almighty, who guided us through you, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said: “You have spoken the truth.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then asked: “Through what qualities did you defeat those who fought you during the pre-Islamic period?”
They replied, “We did not defeat anyone.”
He said: “Indeed, you did defeat those who fought you.”
They replied, “We defeated those who fought us, O Messenger of Allah, because we remained united and did not divide, and we never initiated injustice against anyone.”
He said: “You have spoken the truth.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Qays ibn al-Ḥuṣayn as leader over Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb.
The delegation of Banū al-Ḥārith returned to their people during the remaining days of Shawwāl or at the beginning of Dhū al-Qaʿdah.
Only four months passed after their return before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died—may Allah bestow mercy, blessings, pleasure, and favor upon him.

بعث رسول الله ﷺ غالب بن عبد الله الليثي إلى الميفعة في شهر رمضان سنة سبع من مهاجر رسول الله ﷺ.
قالوا: بعث رسول الله ﷺ غالب بن عبد الله إلى بني عُوال وبني عبد بن ثعلبة، وهم بالميفعة، وهي وراء بطن نخل إلى النُّقرة قليلًا بناحية نجد، وبينها وبين المدينة ثمانية بُرُد.
بعثه في مائة وثلاثين رجلًا، ودليلهم يسار مولى رسول الله ﷺ.
فهجموا عليهم جميعًا، ووقعوا وسط محالِّهم، فقتلوا من أشرف لهم، واستاقوا نعمًا وشاءً، فانحدروا به إلى المدينة، ولم يأسروا أحدًا.
وفي هذه السرية قتل أسامة بن زيد الرجل الذي قال: لا إله إلا الله، فقال النبي ﷺ: «أفلا شققت عن قلبه، فتعلم أصادق هو أم كاذب؟».
فقال أسامة: لا أقاتل أحدًا يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله.
الطبقات الكبرى لابن سعد (٢/١١٩).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ghālib ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Laythī to al-Mayfaʿah in Ramaḍān of the seventh year after the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ghālib ibn ʿAbdullāh against Banū ʿUwāl and Banū ʿAbd ibn Thaʿlabah, who were at al-Mayfaʿah. It lay beyond Baṭn Nakhl, a short distance toward al-Nuqrah in the region of Najd, and was eight postal stages from Madinah.
He sent him with one hundred and thirty men. Their guide was Yasār, a freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They launched a surprise attack upon them and entered the midst of their dwellings. They killed those who came out to confront them, drove away camels and sheep and returned with them to Madinah. They did not take anyone captive.
During this expedition, Usāmah ibn Zayd killed a man who had declared, “There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.” The Prophet ﷺ said to him, “Why did you not open his heart so that you could know whether he was truthful or lying?”
Usāmah then said, “I shall never fight anyone who testifies that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.”
Al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā by Ibn Saʿd (2/119).
The full report of Usāmah follows:

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال ابن هشام: فذكر عبد الله بن جعفر بن عبد الرحمن بن المسور بن مخرمة، عن أبي عون، قال: كان من أمر بني قينقاع أن امرأة من العرب قدمت بجلب لها، فباعته بسوق بني قينقاع، وجلست إلى صائغ هناك منهم، فجعلوا يريدونها على كشف وجهها، فأبت، فعمد الصائغ إلى طرف ثوبها فعقده إلى ظهرها، فلما قامت انكشفت سوأتها، فضحكوا بها، فصاحت، فوثب رجل من المسلمين على الصائغ فقتله، وكان يهوديًّا، فشدت اليهود على المسلم فقتلوه، فاستصرخ أهل المسلم المسلمين على اليهود، فغضب المسلمون، فوقع الشر بينهم وبين بني قينقاع.
قال ابن إسحاق: فحدثني عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة قال: فحاصرهم رسول الله ﷺ حتى نزلوا على حكمه، فقام إليه عبد الله بن أبي ابن سلول، حين أمكنه الله منهم، فقال: يا محمد، أحسن في مواليّ. وكانوا حلفاء الخزرج. قال: فأبطأ عليه رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا محمد، أحسن في مواليّ. قال: فأعرض عنه. قال: فأدخل يده في جيب درع النبي ﷺ، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: «أرسلني». وغضب رسول الله ﷺ حتى رأوا لوجهه ظللًا، ثم قال: «ويحك، أرسلني». قال: لا والله، لا أرسلك حتى تحسن في مواليّ، أربعمائة حاسر وثلاثمائة دارع، قد منعوني من الأحمر والأسود، تحصدهم في غداة واحدة؟ إني والله امرؤ أخشى الدوائر. قال: فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: «هم لك».
قال محمد بن إسحاق: وحدثني عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة: أن بني قينقاع كانوا أول يهود نقضوا ما بينهم وبين رسول الله ﷺ، وحاربوا فيما بين بدر وأحد. سيرة ابن هشام (٢/٤٧).
قال الحافظ ابن القيم: كان للنبي ﷺ مع اليهود أربع غزوات: أولها غزوة بني قينقاع بعد بدر، والثانية بني النضير بعد أحد، والثالثة قريظة بعد الخندق، والرابعة خيبر بعد الحديبية. انظر: زاد المعاد (٣/٢٤٩).
قال ابن سعد: حاصرهم خمس عشرة ليلة إلى هلال ذي القعدة، فكانوا أول من غدر من اليهود وحاربوا، وتحصنوا في حصنهم، فحاصرهم أشد الحصار حتى قذف الله في قلوبهم الرعب، فنزلوا على حكم رسول الله ﷺ: أن لرسول الله ﷺ أموالهم، وأن لهم النساء والذرية. فأمر بهم فكتفوا، واستعمل رسول الله ﷺ على كتافهم المنذر بن قدامة السلمي من بني السلم، رهط سعد بن خيثمة. فكلم فيهم عبد الله بن أبي رسول الله ﷺ، وألح عليه، فقال: خلّوهم، لعنهم الله، ولعنه معهم. وتركهم من القتل، وأمر بهم أن يجلوا من المدينة، وتولى إخراجهم منها عبادة بن الصامت. فلحقوا بأذرعات، فما كان أقل بقاءهم بها. الطبقات الكبرى لابن سعد (٢/٢٩).

Ibn Hishām said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhramah narrated from Abū ʿAwn, who said: The matter of Banū Qaynuqāʿ was that an Arab woman came with goods of hers and sold them in the market of Banū Qaynuqāʿ. She sat with one of their jewelers there, and they tried to make her uncover her face, but she refused. The jeweler went to the end of her garment and tied it to her back. When she stood up, her private area was exposed, and they laughed at her. She cried out, and a Muslim man leapt upon the jeweler and killed him, and he was a Jew. The Jews then attacked the Muslim and killed him. The family of the Muslim called the Muslims for help against the Jews, so the Muslims became angry, and evil broke out between them and Banū Qaynuqāʿ.
Ibn Isḥāq said: ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah narrated to me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them until they submitted to his judgment. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl stood before him when Allah had given him power over them and said, “O Muhammad, be good to my allies.” They were allies of the Khazraj. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed responding to him. He said, “O Muhammad, be good to my allies.” He turned away from him. He put his hand into the opening of the Prophet’s ﷺ armor, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, “Let me go.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until they saw shadows on his face. Then he said, “Woe to you, let me go.” He said, “No, by Allah, I will not let you go until you treat my allies well: four hundred without armor and three hundred armored men. They protected me from the red and the black; will you harvest them in a single morning? By Allah, I am a man who fears turns of fortune.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, “They are yours.”
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah narrated to me that Banū Qaynuqāʿ were the first of the Jews to break what was between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to wage war between Badr and Uḥud. Sīrat Ibn Hishām (2/47).
Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn al-Qayyim said: The Prophet ﷺ had four campaigns against the Jews: the first was the campaign of Banū Qaynuqāʿ after Badr, the second Banū al-Naḍīr after Uḥud, the third Qurayẓah after al-Khandaq, and the fourth Khaybar after al-Ḥudaybiyyah. See Zād al-Maʿād (3/249).
Ibn Saʿd said: He besieged them for fifteen nights until the crescent of Dhū al-Qaʿdah. They were the first of the Jews to act treacherously and wage war, and they fortified themselves in their fortress. He besieged them intensely until Allah cast terror into their hearts, so they submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that their wealth would belong to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while their women and children would remain theirs. He ordered them to be bound, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed al-Mundhir ibn Qudāmah al-Sulamī, from Banū al-Salam, the clan of Saʿd ibn Khaythamah, over binding them. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning them and insisted. He said, “Release them—may Allah curse them and curse him along with them.” He spared them from killing and ordered that they be expelled from Madinah. ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit took charge of expelling them from it. They went to Adhriʿāt, and their stay there was very brief. Al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā of Ibn Saʿd (2/29).

Ibn Hishām said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhramah narrated from Abū ʿAwn, who said: The matter of Banū Qaynuqāʿ was that an Arab woman came with goods of hers and sold them in the market of Banū Qaynuqāʿ. She sat with one of their jewelers there, and they tried to make her uncover her face, but she refused. The jeweler went to the end of her garment and tied it to her back. When she stood up, her private area was exposed, and they laughed at her. She cried out, and a Muslim man leapt upon the jeweler and killed him, and he was a Jew. The Jews then attacked the Muslim and killed him. The family of the Muslim called the Muslims for help against the Jews, so the Muslims became angry, and evil broke out between them and Banū Qaynuqāʿ.
Ibn Isḥāq said: ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah narrated to me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged them until they submitted to his judgment. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl stood before him when Allah had given him power over them and said, “O Muhammad, be good to my allies.” They were allies of the Khazraj. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed responding to him. He said, “O Muhammad, be good to my allies.” He turned away from him. He put his hand into the opening of the Prophet’s ﷺ armor, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, “Let me go.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until they saw shadows on his face. Then he said, “Woe to you, let me go.” He said, “No, by Allah, I will not let you go until you treat my allies well: four hundred without armor and three hundred armored men. They protected me from the red and the black; will you harvest them in a single morning? By Allah, I am a man who fears turns of fortune.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, “They are yours.”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى:
 ﴿كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَيْتِكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَكَارِهُونَ ۝ يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي الْحَقِّ بَعْدَ مَا تَبَيَّنَ كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى الْمَوْتِ وَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ ۝ وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذَاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ وَيُرِيدُ اللهُ أَنْ يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَيَقْطَعَ دَابِرَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ [الأنفال: ٥-٧]
والمراد بالطائفتين: إحداهما عير أبي سفيان، والأخرى جيش قريش.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High said: “Just as your Lord brought you out from your home in truth, while indeed a party among the believers disliked it, arguing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear, as if they were being driven toward death while looking on. And when Allah promised you one of the two groups that it would be yours, and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours, but Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the root of the disbelievers.” [al-Anfāl: 5-7]
The two groups referred to are: the caravan of Abū Sufyān and the army of Quraysh.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
كانت في شهر ربيع الآخر سنة ست من مهاجر رسول الله ﷺ. بعث رسول الله ﷺ محمد بن مسلمة إلى بني ثعلبة وبني عوال من ثعلبة، وهم بذي القصة، وبينها وبين المدينة أربعة وعشرون ميلًا على طريق الربذة، في عشرة نفر.
فوردوا عليهم ليلًا، فأحدق بهم القوم، وهم مائة رجل. فتراموا ساعة من الليل، ثم حملت الأعراب عليهم بالرماح فقتلوهم. ووقع محمد بن مسلمة جريحًا، فضربوا كعبه فلم يتحرك، وجردوهم من الثياب.
ومر بمحمد بن مسلمة رجل من المسلمين فحمله حتى ورد به المدينة. فبعث رسول الله ﷺ أبا عبيدة بن الجراح في أربعين رجلًا إلى مصارع القوم، فلم يجدوا أحدًا، ووجدوا نعمًا وشاءً، فساقوه ورجعوا. «الطبقات الكبرى» لابن سعد (٢/٨٥).

chapters.intro_en_source:
It took place in Rabīʿ al-Ākhir of the sixth year after the Messenger of Allah’s emigration. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Muḥammad ibn Maslamah with ten men against Banū Thaʿlabah and Banū ʿAwāl, a branch of Thaʿlabah, at Dhū al-Qaṣṣah. It lay twenty-four miles from Madinah along the road to al-Rabadhah.
They reached them at night, but approximately one hundred men surrounded them. They exchanged arrows for part of the night, after which the Bedouins charged them with spears and killed them. Muḥammad ibn Maslamah fell wounded. They struck his heel, but he did not move, so they assumed he was dead and stripped the men of their clothing.
A Muslim later passed by Muḥammad ibn Maslamah and carried him back to Madinah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ with forty men to the place where the expedition had fallen. They found no one there but discovered camels and sheep, which they drove back with them. Al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā by Ibn Saʿd (2/85).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال ابن إسحاق: “وبعث رسول الله ﷺ في مقامه ذلك بالمدينة عبيدة بن الحارث بن المطلب بن عبد مناف بن قصي في ستين أو ثمانين راكبًا من المهاجرين، ليس فيهم من الأنصار أحد، فسار حتى بلغ ماءً بالحجاز بأسفل ثنية المرة، فلقي بها جمعًا عظيمًا من قريش، فلم يكن بينهم قتال، إلا أن سعد بن أبي وقاص قد رمى يومئذ بسهم، فكان أول سهم رمي به في الإسلام. وفي هذه السرية فرّ من المشركين إلى المسلمين المقداد بن عمرو البهراني، وعتبة بن غزوان بن جابر المازني، وكانا مسلمين، ولكنهما خرجا ليتوصلا بالكفار، وكان على القوم عكرمة بن أبي جهل.”
سيرة ابن هشام (٥٩١-٥٩٢/١).
وقوله: “ليتوصلا بالكفار” أي أنهما جعلا خروجهما مع الكفار وسيلة للوصول إلى المسلمين.

Ibn Isḥāq said: “While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was residing in Madinah, he sent ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy with sixty or eighty riders from the Muhājirūn; there was not a single Anṣārī among them. He traveled until he reached a water-place in the Ḥijāz below Thaniyyat al-Murrah. There he met a large group of Quraysh, but there was no fighting between them, except that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ shot an arrow that day, and it was the first arrow shot in Islam. In this detachment, al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr al-Bahrānī and ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān ibn Jābir al-Māzinī fled from the polytheists to the Muslims. They were already Muslims, but they had gone out in order to use the disbelievers as a means of reaching the Muslims. ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl was the commander of the enemy group.”
Sīrat Ibn Hishām (1/591-592).
The phrase “to use the disbelievers as a means” means that they made their departure with the disbelievers a way to reach the Muslims.

وهي أكبر بناته ﷺ. ولدت قبل البعثة بمدة، وهي أول من تزوج من بناته ﷺ. تزوجها أبو العاص بن الربيع العبشمي، ابن خالتها هالة بنت خويلد، قبل الإسلام.
ولما جاء الإسلام أسلمت، وأبى زوجها أبو العاص أن يسلم. ولما جاء وقت الهجرة إلى المدينة هاجرت أخواتها، وبقيت هي في مكة. وأسر زوجها أبو العاص في بدر، فبعثت زينب في فدائه بمال فيه قلادة لها كانت عند خديجة، وكانت خديجة أدخلتها بها على أبي العاص. فلما رآها رسول الله ﷺ رق لها رقة شديدة، فأشار على الصحابة بإطلاق سراحه فاستجابوا له، وأخذ عليه رسول الله ﷺ أن يخلي سبيل زينب إليه.
فلما قدم مكة أمر زينب باللحوق بأبيها. فخرجت، فتعرض لها بذي طوى هبار بن الأسود، فلم يزل يطعن بعيرها برمحه حتى صرعها، وكانت حاملًا، فألقت ما في بطنها، وأهريقت دمًا. وواصلت مسيرها حتى لحقت أباها بالمدينة.
ثم أسلم أبو العاص في المحرم سنة سبع، فرد عليه رسول الله ﷺ زينب بالنكاح الأول.
وتوفيت زينب في أول سنة ثمان من الهجرة، وصلى عليها أبوها، ودفنت بالبقيع. وكانت زينب ولدت من أبي العاص عليًّا وأمامة. أما علي فمات وقد ناهز الاحتلام، وأما أمامة فعاشت حتى تزوجها علي بعد موت خالتها فاطمة، ولم تلد، فليس لزينب عقب.
انظر: الإصابة (١١٣٥٤).

ولما جاء الإسلام أسلمت، وأبى زوجها أبو العاص أن يسلم. ولما جاء وقت الهجرة إلى المدينة هاجرت أخواتها، وبقيت هي في مكة. وأسر زوجها أبو العاص في بدر، فبعثت زينب في فدائه بمال فيه قلادة لها كانت عند خديجة، وكانت خديجة أدخلتها بها على أبي العاص. فلما رآها رسول الله ﷺ رق لها رقة شديدة، فأشار على الصحابة بإطلاق سراحه فاستجابوا له، وأخذ عليه رسول الله ﷺ أن يخلي سبيل زينب إليه.
فلما قدم مكة أمر زينب باللحوق بأبيها. فخرجت، فتعرض لها بذي طوى هبار بن الأسود، فلم يزل يطعن بعيرها برمحه حتى صرعها، وكانت حاملًا، فألقت ما في بطنها، وأهريقت دمًا. وواصلت مسيرها حتى لحقت أباها بالمدينة.
ثم أسلم أبو العاص في المحرم سنة سبع، فرد عليه رسول الله ﷺ زينب بالنكاح الأول.
وتوفيت زينب في أول سنة ثمان من الهجرة، وصلى عليها أبوها، ودفنت بالبقيع. وكانت زينب ولدت من أبي العاص عليًّا وأمامة. أما علي فمات وقد ناهز الاحتلام، وأما أمامة فعاشت حتى تزوجها علي بعد موت خالتها فاطمة، ولم تلد، فليس لزينب عقب.
انظر: الإصابة (١١٣٥٤).
chapters.intro_en_source:
She was the eldest of the Prophet’s ﷺ daughters. She was born some time before the beginning of prophethood and was the first of his daughters to marry. Before Islam, she married Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ al-ʿAbshamī, the son of her maternal aunt Hālah bint Khuwaylid.
When Islam came, Zaynab embraced it, but her husband Abū al-ʿĀṣ refused to accept Islam. When the Muslims migrated to Madinah, her sisters migrated while she remained in Makkah.
Her husband, Abū al-ʿĀṣ, was taken captive at Badr. Zaynab sent property to ransom him, including a necklace that had belonged to Khadījah and that Khadījah had given her when she entered into marriage with Abū al-ʿĀṣ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it, he was deeply moved. He suggested that the Companions release Abū al-ʿĀṣ, and they agreed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ required him in return to allow Zaynab to join her father.
When Abū al-ʿĀṣ returned to Makkah, he instructed Zaynab to join her father. She set out, but Habbār ibn al-Aswad confronted her at Dhū Ṭuwā and continued prodding her camel with his spear until she was thrown from it. She was pregnant and miscarried, suffering severe bleeding. Nevertheless, she continued her journey until she joined her father in Madinah.
Abū al-ʿĀṣ embraced Islam in Muḥarram of the seventh year after the Hijrah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ restored Zaynab to him under their original marriage contract.
Zaynab died at the beginning of the eighth year after the Hijrah. Her father performed her funeral prayer, and she was buried in al-Baqīʿ. She bore Abū al-ʿĀṣ two children: ʿAlī and Umāmah. ʿAlī died when he had nearly reached puberty. Umāmah lived until ʿAlī married her after the death of her maternal aunt Fāṭimah, but she bore no children. Zaynab therefore left no surviving descendants.
See: Al-Iṣābah (11354).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الزهري: بعث رسول الله ﷺ كعب بن عمير الغفاري في خمسة عشر رجلًا، حتى انتهوا إلى ذات أطلاح من أرض الشام.
فوجدوا جمعًا من جمعهم كثيرًا، فدعوهم إلى الإسلام، فلم يستجيبوا لهم، ورشقوهم بالنبل.
فلما رأى ذلك أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ قاتلوهم أشد القتال حتى قُتلوا.
فأفلت منهم رجل جريح في القتلى، فلما أن برد عليه الليل تحامل حتى أتى رسول الله ﷺ.
فهمّ بالبعثة إليهم، فبلغه أنهم ساروا إلى موضع آخر فتركهم.
رواه الواقدي في المغازي (٢/٧٥٢–٧٥٣)، قال: حدثني محمد بن عبد الله، عن الزهري، فذكره.
وقال: حدثني ابن أبي سبرة، عن الحارث بن الفضيل، قال: كان كعب يكمن النهار ويسير الليل حتى دنا منهم، فرآه عين لهم فأخبرهم بقلة أصحاب النبي ﷺ، فجاؤوا على الخيول فقتلوهم.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Al-Zuhrī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Kaʿb ibn ʿUmayr al-Ghifārī with fifteen men. They travelled until they reached Dhāt Aṭlāḥ in the region of al-Shām.
They encountered a large force belonging to them and invited them to Islam, but they refused to respond and showered the Muslims with arrows.
When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw this, they fought them with the greatest intensity until they were killed.
One wounded man survived among the bodies of the slain. When the coolness of night arrived, he forced himself onward until he reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to send another force against them, but he learned that they had moved elsewhere, so he left them.
Al-Wāqidī narrated it in al-Maghāzī (2/752–753), saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to me from al-Zuhrī, and he related the report.
He also said: Ibn Abī Sabrah narrated to me from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said: Kaʿb concealed his force during the day and travelled by night until he drew near to them. One of their scouts saw him and informed them that the Prophet’s ﷺ Companions were few in number. They therefore came on horseback and killed them.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
كانت سرية الضحاك بن سفيان الكلابي إلى بني كلاب في شهر ربيع الأول سنة تسع من مهاجر رسول الله ﷺ.
قالوا: بعث رسول الله ﷺ جيشًا إلى القرطاء، عليهم الضحاك بن سفيان بن عوف بن أبي بكر الكلابي، ومعه الأصيد بن سلمة بن قرط.
فلقوهم بالزج، زج لاوة، فدعوهم إلى الإسلام فأبوا، فقاتلوهم فهزموهم.
فلحق الأصيد أباه سلمة، وسلمة على فرس له في غدير بالزج. فدعا أباه إلى الإسلام وأعطاه الأمان، فسبه وسب دينه.
فضرب الأصيد عرقوبي فرس أبيه. فلما وقع الفرس على عرقوبيه، ارتكز سلمة على رمحه في الماء، ثم استمسك به حتى جاءه أحدهم فقتله، ولم يقتله ابنه.
طبقات ابن سعد (١٦٢–١٦٣/٢).

chapters.intro_en_source:
The expedition of al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Sufyān al-Kilābī against Banū Kilāb took place during Rabīʿ al-Awwal in the ninth year after the migration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent an army against al-Quraṭāʾ under the command of al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Sufyān ibn ʿAwf ibn Abī Bakr al-Kilābī. Al-Uṣayd ibn Salamah ibn Qurṭ accompanied him.
They encountered them at al-Zujj—Zujj Lāwah—and invited them to Islam, but they refused. The Muslims fought and defeated them.
Al-Uṣayd caught up with his father Salamah, who was mounted upon a horse in a pool of water at al-Zujj. Al-Uṣayd invited his father to Islam and offered him protection, but his father insulted him and his religion.
Al-Uṣayd struck the hocks of his father’s horse. When the horse collapsed upon its hind legs, Salamah planted his spear in the water and held on to it until another Muslim came and killed him. His son did not kill him.
Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd (2/162–163).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
كانت سرية سعد بن زيد الأشهلي إلى مناة بالمشلل، في شهر رمضان سنة ثمان من مهاجر رسول الله ﷺ.
قالوا: لما فتح رسول الله ﷺ مكة، بعث سعد بن زيد الأشهلي إلى مناة، صنم الأوس والخزرج، وهي بالمشلل ناحية قديد، في عشرين فارسًا، فهدمها.
فلما انتهى إليها قال له سادنها: ما تريد؟
قال: هدم مناة.
قال: أنت وذاك.
فأقبل سعد يمشي إليها، فخرجت إليه امرأة سوداء عريانة ثائرة الرأس تدعو بالويل وتضرب صدرها.
فقال السادن: مناة دونك بعض عصاتك.
فضربها سعد بن زيد فقتلها، وأقبل إلى الصنم ومعه أصحابه، فهدموه.
ولم يجدوا في خزانتها شيئًا، وانصرف راجعًا إلى رسول الله ﷺ.
وكان ذلك لست بقين من شهر رمضان.
طبقات ابن سعد (٢/١٤٦–١٤٧).

chapters.intro_en_source:
The expedition of Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ashhalī to Manāt at al-Mushallal took place in Ramaḍān of the eighth year after the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Makkah, he sent Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ashhalī with twenty horsemen to Manāt, the idol of the Aws and Khazraj, located at al-Mushallal near Qudayd, and he destroyed it.
When he reached it, its custodian asked him, “What do you want?”
He replied, “To destroy Manāt.”
The custodian said, “That is between you and it.”
Saʿd advanced toward it, whereupon a black, naked woman with disheveled hair came out toward him, wailing and striking her chest.
The custodian said, “Manāt, here is one of your disobedient enemies before you.”
Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ashhalī struck and killed her. He and his companions then approached the idol and demolished it.
They found nothing in its treasury and returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
This took place when six nights remained of Ramaḍān.
Ibn Saʿd’s al-Ṭabaqāt (2/146–147).

وكان يقال لها أم المساكين؛ لأنها كانت تطعمهم وتتصدق عليهم. وكانت تحت عبد الله بن جحش، فاستشهد بأحد، فتزوجها النبي ﷺ. وقيل: كانت عند الطفيل بن الحارث بن عبد المطلب، ثم خلف عليها أخوه عبيدة بن الحارث. وكانت أخت ميمونة بنت الحارث لأمها.
وكان دخوله ﷺ بها بعد دخوله على حفصة بنت عمر، ثم لم تلبث عنده إلا شهرين أو ثلاثة، وماتت. قاله ابن حجر في الإصابة (١١٣٦٧).

She was known as “the Mother of the Needy” because she used to feed the poor and give charity to them. She had been married to ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaḥsh, who was martyred at Uḥud, after which the Prophet ﷺ married her.
It has also been said that she was first married to al-Ṭufayl ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and that his brother ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith married her afterward. She was the maternal half-sister of Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith.
The Prophet ﷺ consummated his marriage with her after his marriage to Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar. She remained with him for only two or three months before she died. This was stated by Ibn Ḥajar in Al-Iṣābah (11367).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قالوا: بعث رسول الله ﷺ عليًّا إلى اليمن، وعقد له لواء، وعممه بيده، وقال:
«امض ولا تلتفت، فإذا نزلت بساحتهم فلا تقاتلهم حتى يقاتلوك».
فخرج في ثلاثمائة فارس، وكانت أول خيل دخلت إلى تلك البلاد، وهي بلاد مذحج.
ففرق أصحابه، فأتوا بنهب وغنائم ونساء وأطفال ونعم وشاء وغير ذلك.
وجعل علي على الغنائم بريدة بن الحصيب الأسلمي، فجمع إليه ما أصابوا.
ثم لقي جمعهم فدعاهم إلى الإسلام، فأبوا ورموا بالنبل والحجارة.
فصف أصحابه، ودفع لواءه إلى مسعود بن سنان السلمي، ثم حمل عليهم علي بأصحابه، فقتل منهم عشرين رجلًا، فتفرقوا وانهزموا.
فكف عن طلبهم، ثم دعاهم إلى الإسلام، فأسرعوا وأجابوا.
وبايعه نفر من رؤسائهم على الإسلام، وقالوا: نحن على من وراءنا من قومنا، وهذه صدقاتنا، فخذ منها حق الله.
وجمع علي الغنائم فجزأها على خمسة أجزاء، فكتب في سهم منها: لله، وأقرع عليها، فخرج أول السهام سهم الخمس.
وقسم علي على أصحابه بقية المغنم، ثم قفل، فوافى النبي ﷺ بمكة، وقد قدمها للحج سنة عشر.
الطبقات الكبرى (١٦٩–١٧٠/٢).

chapters.intro_en_source:
They said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAlī to Yemen, tied a banner for him, wrapped his turban around his head with his own hand, and said:
“Proceed without looking back. When you reach their territory, do not fight them unless they fight you.”
He set out with three hundred horsemen. They were the first cavalry force to enter that region, which was the territory of Madhḥij.
He dispersed his companions in different directions, and they returned with captured property, spoils, women, children, camels, sheep, and other things.
ʿAlī appointed Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb al-Aslamī to supervise the spoils, and Buraydah gathered everything they acquired.
He then encountered their assembled forces and invited them to Islam, but they refused and shot arrows and threw stones at the Muslims.
ʿAlī arranged his companions in ranks and handed his banner to Masʿūd ibn Sinān al-Sulamī. He and his companions then charged them and killed twenty of their men, whereupon they scattered and fled.
ʿAlī refrained from pursuing them and again invited them to Islam. They quickly responded and accepted.
A group of their leaders pledged allegiance to him upon Islam and said, “We speak on behalf of the members of our tribe behind us. These are our charitable dues, so take from them the right ordained by Allah.”
ʿAlī gathered the spoils and divided them into five portions. Upon one portion he wrote, “For Allah,” and then drew lots. The first lot drawn was the one-fifth.
ʿAlī distributed the remainder of the spoils among his companions and then returned. He met the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah, where the Prophet had arrived to perform pilgrimage in the tenth year.
Al-Ṭabaqāt al-Kubrā (2/169–170).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
كانت سرية علي بن أبي طالب إلى الفُلْس، صنم طيئ، ليهدمه في شهر ربيع الآخر سنة تسع من مهاجر رسول الله ﷺ.
قالوا: بعث رسول الله ﷺ علي بن أبي طالب في خمسين ومائة رجل من الأنصار، على مائة بعير وخمسين فرسًا، ومعه راية سوداء ولواء أبيض، إلى الفلس ليهدمه.
فشنوا الغارة على محلة آل حاتم مع الفجر، فهدموا الفلس وخربوه، وملؤوا أيديهم من السبي والنعم والشاء.
وفي السبي أخت عدي بن حاتم، وهرب عدي إلى الشام.
ووجد في خزانة الفلس ثلاثة أسياف: رسوب، والمخذم، وسيف يقال له اليماني، وثلاثة أدراع.
واستعمل رسول الله ﷺ على السبي أبا قتادة، واستعمل على الماشية والرثة عبد الله بن عتيك.
فلما نزلوا ركك اقتسموا الغنائم، وعزل للنبي ﷺ صفيًّا رسوبًا والمخذم، ثم صار له بعد السيف الآخر. وعزل الخمس، وعزل آل حاتم، فلم يقسمهم حتى قدم بهم المدينة.
طبقات ابن سعد (١٦٤/٢).

chapters.intro_en_source:
The expedition of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib to destroy al-Fuls, the idol of Ṭayyiʾ, took place during Rabīʿ al-Ākhir in the ninth year after the migration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib with one hundred and fifty men from the Anṣār, riding one hundred camels and fifty horses. He carried a black standard and a white banner and was sent to destroy al-Fuls.
They attacked the settlement of the family of Ḥātim at dawn, demolished al-Fuls, and destroyed its structure. They acquired numerous captives, camels, and sheep.
Among the captives was the sister of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, while ʿAdī himself fled to Syria.
Three swords were found in the treasury of al-Fuls: Rasūb, al-Mikhdham, and a sword called al-Yamānī, together with three suits of armor.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Abū Qatādah to supervise the captives and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAtīk to supervise the livestock and other goods.
When they stopped at Rukak, they divided the spoils. Rasūb and al-Mikhdham were set aside as the Prophet’s ﷺ chosen share, and the other sword later came into his possession as well. One-fifth was also set aside. The family of Ḥātim was kept apart and not distributed until they were brought to Madinah.
Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd (2/164).

chapters.intro_en_source:
Al-Wāqidī mentioned that they arrived in the ninth year, when the Prophet ﷺ was returning from Tabūk. They were thirteen men, led by al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf. The Prophet ﷺ rewarded each of them with ten awqiyahs of silver and gave al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf twelve awqiyahs.
They mentioned that their land was suffering from drought, so he supplicated for them, saying:
“O Allah, grant them abundant rain.”
When they returned to their homeland, they found that rain had fallen there on the very day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had supplicated for them.
Narrated by Ibn Saʿd in al-Ṭabaqāt (1/297–298), from al-Wāqidī.
chapters.intro_en_display:
Al-Wāqidī mentioned that they arrived in the ninth year, when the Prophet ﷺ was returning from Tabūk. They were thirteen men, led by al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf. The Prophet ﷺ rewarded each of them with ten awqiyahs of silver and gave al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf twelve awqiyahs.
They mentioned that their land was suffering from drought, so he supplicated for them, saying:
“O Allah, grant them abundant rain.”
When they returned to their homeland, they found that rain had fallen there on the very day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had supplicated for them.
Narrated by Ibn Saʿd in al-Ṭabaqāt (1/297–298), from al-Wāqidī.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال الله تعالى:
﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَلَا أَنْ تَنْكِحُوا أَزْوَاجَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أَبَدًا﴾ [الأحزاب: ٥٣].
قول الله تعالى: ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أَبَدًا﴾ يحمل على وفاته، وأشمل منه: بعد نكاحه؛ فإنهن بمجرد نكاح النبي ﷺ صرن من أمهات المؤمنين في حياته ﷺ وبعد مماته. والأمومة المقصود بها الاحترام والإجلال، لا مثل الأم الحقيقية التي يجوز الدخول عليها والخلوة بها، وتحرم بناتها على أبنائها. فيقتصر حكم الأمومة على تحريم نكاحهن بعد وفاته ﷺ.
وأما بقية أحكام التحريم فلا يشملها، مثل نكاح بناته ﷺ، فإنه يجوز للمسلم أن يتزوج بهن.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High says:
“It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor ever to marry his wives after him.” [Al-Aḥzāb: 53]
The words of Allah Most High, “after him, ever,” may be understood as referring to after his death. More comprehensively, however, they apply from the time he married them. As soon as the Prophet ﷺ married them, they became Mothers of the Believers, both during his lifetime and after his death.
The motherhood intended here is one of respect and veneration. It is not identical to biological motherhood, in which a person may freely enter upon his mother and be alone with her, while her daughters are forbidden in marriage to her sons. The ruling of motherhood here is therefore restricted to the prohibition of marrying the Prophet’s wives after his death ﷺ.
The remaining marital prohibitions associated with biological motherhood do not apply. For example, it was permissible for a Muslim man to marry one of the Prophet’s daughters ﷺ.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
رقية ولدت قبل البعثة، وتزوجت من عتبة بن أبي لهب. فلما نزل قوله تعالى: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ﴾ [المسد: ١] طلقها عتبة، ولم يكن دخل بها.
فزوجها رسول الله ﷺ عثمان بن عفان بمكة، وهاجر بها عثمان إلى الحبشة، ثم رجعا إلى مكة، وهاجرا إلى المدينة.
ومرضت لما خرج رسول الله ﷺ إلى بدر، فتخلف عليها عثمان عن بدر بإذن رسول الله ﷺ. فماتت بعد أيام ورسول الله ﷺ في بدر، ودفنت بالبقيع. وقد سووا عليها التراب حين وصل بشير رسول الله ﷺ بالانتصار في بدر.
وكانت ولدت لعثمان عبد الله، وبه كان يكنى، فنقره ديك في عينيه فمات وهو صغير، ولم تلد له بعد ذلك، فليس لرقية عقب.
انظر: الإصابة (١١٣١٨)، وسبل الهدى (٣٣–٣٥/١١).

chapters.intro_en_source:
Ruqayyah was born before the beginning of prophethood and married ʿUtbah ibn Abī Lahab. When Allah Most High revealed, “May the hands of Abū Lahab perish, and may he perish!” [Al-Masad: 1], ʿUtbah divorced her before consummating the marriage.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then married her to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān in Makkah. ʿUthmān took her with him when he migrated to Abyssinia. They later returned to Makkah and then migrated to Madinah.
She fell ill when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed for Badr. With the Messenger of Allah’s ﷺ permission, ʿUthmān remained behind to care for her and did not participate in the battle. She died several days later while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at Badr and was buried in al-Baqīʿ. The earth over her grave had just been leveled when the Messenger of Allah’s ﷺ herald arrived with news of the victory at Badr.
She bore ʿUthmān a son named ʿAbdullāh, after whom he took his agnomen Abū ʿAbdullāh. A rooster pecked ʿAbdullāh in the eye, and he died while still young. Ruqayyah bore no other children, and therefore left no surviving descendants.
See: Al-Iṣābah (11318) and Subul al-Hudā (11/33–35).

chapters.intro_ar_source: قال ابن إسحاق: ثم غزا أبو سفيان بن حرب غزوة السويق في ذي الحجة، في السنة الثانية من الهجرة. وذلك أن أبا سفيان بن حرب لما رجع المشركون من بدر إلى مكة حرم الدهن حتى يثأر من محمد وأصحابه، فخرج في مائتي راكب في حديث الزهري، وفي حديث ابن كعب: في أربعين راكبًا، فسلكوا النجدية، فجاؤوا إلى بني النضير ليلًا، فطرقوا حيي بن أخطب، فأبى أن يفتح لهم بابه، فطرقوا سلام بن مشكم، ففتح لهم وقراهم، وسقاهم خمرًا، وأخبرهم من أخبار رسول الله ﷺ. فلما كان بالسحر خرج أبو سفيان بن حرب، فمر بالعريض، وبينه وبين المدينة نحو من ثلاثة أميال، فقتل به رجلًا من الأنصار وأجيرًا له، وحرق أبياتًا هناك وتبنًا، ورأى أن يمينه قد حلت، ثم ولى هاربًا. فبلغ ذلك رسول الله ﷺ، فندب أصحابه، وخرج في مائتي رجل من المهاجرين والأنصار في أثرهم يطلبهم، وجعل أبو سفيان وأصحابه يتخففون فيلقون جرب السويق، وهي عامة أزوادهم، فجعل المسلمون يأخذونها، فسميت غزوة السويق. ولم يلحقوهم، وانصرف رسول الله ﷺ إلى المدينة، وكان غاب خمسة أيام. انظر: سيرة ابن هشام (٢/٤٤)، وطبقات ابن سعد (٢/٣٠).

chapters.intro_en_source: Ibn Isḥāq said: Then Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb carried out the Battle of al-Sawīq in Dhū al-Ḥijjah, in the second year after the Hijrah. That was because when the polytheists returned from Badr to Makkah, Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb forbade himself oil until he took revenge on Muhammad and his Companions. He went out with two hundred riders according to the narration of al-Zuhrī, and in the narration of Ibn Kaʿb: with forty riders. They took the Najd route and came to Banū al-Naḍīr at night. They knocked at the door of Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, but he refused to open his door for them. Then they knocked at the door of Sallām ibn Mishkam, and he opened for them, hosted them, gave them wine to drink, and informed them of the news of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. At dawn, Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb left and passed by al-ʿArīḍ, which was about three miles from Madinah. There he killed a man from the Anṣār and a hired worker of his, burned some houses and fodder there, considered that his oath had been fulfilled, and then fled. That reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he summoned his Companions and went out with two hundred men from the Muhājirūn and Anṣār in pursuit of them. Abū Sufyān and his companions began lightening their loads by throwing away sacks of sawīq, which was most of their provisions, so the Muslims began taking them. For this reason it was called the Battle of al-Sawīq. They did not catch them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to Madinah, having been absent for five days. See Sīrat Ibn Hishām (2/44) and Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd (2/30).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
بعث رسول الله ﷺ زيد بن حارثة إلى مدينة مَقْنَا، وهي تقع قرب أيلة على البحر الأحمر، آخر الحجاز وأول الشام.
فأصابوا منها سبايا، منهم ضميرة مولى علي، فأمر رسول الله ﷺ ببيعهم، وهم إخوة.
فخرج إليهم وهم يبكون، فقال: «ما لهم يبكون؟».
فقالوا: فُرّق بينهم.
قال: «لا تفرّقوا بينهم، بيعوهم جميعًا».
ذكره ابن سعد في القسم المتمم لتابعي أهل المدينة، ص: ٤٥٢، في ترجمة حسين بن عبد الله، بإسناده عن فاطمة بنت الحسين بن علي.
قال الحافظ ابن حجر في الإصابة (٢/٢١٤): سنده منقطع؛ يعني أن فاطمة بنت الحسين لم تدرك النبي ﷺ.
وذكره سعيد بن منصور في سننه (٢/٢٤٨) بإسناده عن فاطمة بنت الحسين، وقال: «مَقْنَا هي مَدْيَن»، وهي تقع غرب تبوك.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Zayd ibn Ḥārithah to the town of Maqnā. It is situated near Aylah on the Red Sea, at the end of the Ḥijāz and the beginning of al-Shām.
They took captives there, among whom was Ḍumayrah, the freedman of ʿAlī. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that they be sold, and they were siblings.
He came out to them while they were weeping and asked, “Why are they crying?”
They replied, “They have been separated from one another.”
He said, “Do not separate them. Sell them together.”
Ibn Saʿd mentioned it in the supplementary section concerning the Successors of Madinah, page 452, in the biography of Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbdullāh, through his chain from Fāṭimah bint al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī.
Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in al-Iṣābah (2/214): “Its chain is disconnected,” meaning that Fāṭimah bint al-Ḥusayn did not live during the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr also mentioned it in his Sunan (2/248), through his chain from Fāṭimah bint al-Ḥusayn, and said: “Maqnā is Madyan.” It is situated west of Tabūk.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr also mentioned it in his Sunan (2/248), through his chain from Fāṭimah bint al-Ḥusayn, and said: “Maqnā is Madyan.” It is situated west of Tabūk.

كانت في شهر ربيع الآخر سنة ست من مهاجر رسول الله ﷺ. أجدبت بلاد بني ثعلبة وأنمار، ووقعت سحابة بالمراض إلى تغلمين، والمراض على ستة وثلاثين ميلًا من المدينة. فسارت بنو محارب وثعلبة وأنمار إلى تلك السحابة.
وأجمعوا أن يغيروا على سرح المدينة، وهو يرعى بهيفاء، موضع على سبعة أميال من المدينة. فبعث رسول الله ﷺ أبا عبيدة بن الجراح في أربعين رجلًا من المسلمين حين صلوا المغرب.
فمشوا إليهم حتى وافوا ذا القصة مع عماية الصبح، فأغاروا عليهم، فأعجزوهم هربًا في الجبال. وأصابوا رجلًا واحدًا فأسلم فتركوه، وأخذوا نعمًا من نعمهم فاستاقوه، ورثَّة من متاعهم.
وقدم بذلك المدينة، فخمسه رسول الله ﷺ، وقسم ما بقي عليهم. «مغازي الواقدي» (٢/٥٥٢)، و«طبقات ابن سعد» (٢/٨٦).

It took place in Rabīʿ al-Ākhir of the sixth year after the Messenger of Allah’s emigration. The lands of Banū Thaʿlabah and Anmār had suffered drought, while rain fell over the region extending from al-Marāḍ to Taghlamayn. Al-Marāḍ was thirty-six miles from Madinah. Banū Muḥārib, Thaʿlabah, and Anmār therefore moved toward the area that had received rain.
They resolved to raid the grazing livestock of Madinah, which were pastured at Hayfāʾ, seven miles from the city. After the Muslims had performed the sunset prayer, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ with forty men.
They traveled on foot until they reached Dhū al-Qaṣṣah in the darkness immediately before dawn. They attacked the people, who escaped them by fleeing into the mountains. They captured one man, but when he embraced Islam, they released him. They took some of the enemy’s camels and a small quantity of worn belongings.
Abū ʿUbaydah brought these things to Madinah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took one-fifth and distributed the remainder among the expedition. Maghāzī al-Wāqidī (2/552) and Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd (2/86).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
بعث رسول الله ﷺ حمزة بن عبد المطلب بن هاشم إلى سيف البحر من ناحية العِيص، في ثلاثين راكبًا من المهاجرين، ليس فيهم من الأنصار أحد، فلقي أبا جهل بن هشام بذلك الساحل في ثلاثمائة راكب من أهل مكة، فحجز بينهم مجدي بن عمرو الجهني، وكان موادعًا للفريقين جميعًا، فانصرف بعض القوم عن بعض، ولم يكن بينهم قتال.
نقل الواقدي في المغازي (١٠/١)، عن ابن المسيب وعبد الرحمن بن سعيد بن يربوع قالا: لم يبعث رسول الله ﷺ أحدًا من الأنصار مبعثًا حتى غزا بنفسه إلى بدر؛ وذلك أنه ظن أنهم لا ينصرونه إلا في الدار.
واختلف أهل السير والتاريخ: أي البعثين كان أولًا؟ فذهب ابن إسحاق إلى أن راية عبيدة بن الحارث كانت أول راية عقدها رسول الله ﷺ. وقال: وبعض الناس يقول: كانت راية حمزة أول راية عقدها رسول الله ﷺ لأحد المسلمين؛ وذلك أن بعثه وبعث عبيدة كانا معًا، فشبه ذلك على الناس.
سيرة ابن هشام (٥٩٥-٥٩٦/١).

chapters.intro_en_source:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim to Sīf al-Baḥr from the direction of al-ʿĪṣ, with thirty riders from the Muhājirūn; there was not a single Anṣārī among them. He met Abū Jahl ibn Hishām on that coast with three hundred riders from the people of Makkah. Majdī ibn ʿAmr al-Juhanī intervened between them, and he had a treaty with both groups, so each side withdrew from the other, and no fighting occurred between them.
Al-Wāqidī transmitted in al-Maghāzī (1/10), from Ibn al-Musayyib and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Yarbūʿ, that they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not send anyone from the Anṣār on a mission until he personally went out to Badr, because he thought they would only support him within their own land.
The scholars of sīrah and history differed regarding which of the two missions came first. Ibn Isḥāq held that the banner of ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith was the first banner that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tied. He said: Some people say that the banner of Ḥamzah was the first banner that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tied for any Muslim, because his dispatch and the dispatch of ʿUbaydah occurred together, so the matter became confused for people.
Sīrat Ibn Hishām (1/595-596).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
ذكر ابن إسحاق أنه كان بعد بئر معونة وأحد، ورجوع عمرو بن أمية، وقتله ذينك الرجلين من بني عامر، ولم يشعر بعهدهما الذي معهما من رسول الله ﷺ. ولهذا قال له رسول الله ﷺ: «لقد قتلت الرجلين لأدينهما».
قال ابن إسحاق: ثم خرج رسول الله ﷺ إلى بني النضير يستعينهم في دية ذينك القتيلين من بني عامر، اللذين قتلهما عمرو بن أمية، للعهد الذي كان رسول الله ﷺ أعطاهما. وكان بين بني النضير وبين بني عامر عقد وحلف.
فلما أتاهم رسول الله ﷺ قالوا: نعم يا أبا القاسم، نعينك على ما أحببت. ثم خلا بعضهم ببعض، فقالوا: إنكم لن تجدوا الرجل على مثل حاله هذه – ورسول الله ﷺ إلى جنب جدار من بيوتهم قاعد – فمن رجل يعلو على هذا البيت، فيلقي عليه صخرة ويريحنا منه؟ فانتدب لذلك عمرو بن جحاش بن كعب، فقال: أنا لذلك. فصعد ليلقي عليه صخرة كما قال.
ورسول الله ﷺ في نفر من أصحابه، فيهم أبو بكر وعمر وعلي، فأتى رسول الله ﷺ الخبر من السماء بما أراد القوم، فقام وخرج راجعًا إلى المدينة. فلما استلبث أصحاب النبي ﷺ النبيَّ قاموا في طلبه، فلقوا رجلًا مقبلًا من المدينة فسألوه عنه، فقال: رأيته داخلًا المدينة. فأقبل أصحابه حتى انتهوا إليه، فأخبرهم الخبر بما كانت يهود أرادت من الغدر به.
وأمر رسول الله ﷺ بالتهيؤ لحربهم والسير إليهم. قال ابن هشام: فحاصرهم ست ليال، ونزل تحريم الخمر.
قال ابن إسحاق: فتحصنوا منه في الحصون، فأمر رسول الله ﷺ بقطع النخيل والتحريق فيها. فنادوه: يا محمد، قد كنت تنهى عن الفساد وتعيبه على من صنعه، فما بال قطع النخل وتحريقها؟
وكان رهط من بني عوف بن الخزرج، منهم عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول، ووديعة، ومالك بن أبي قوقل، وسويد، وداعس، قد بعثوا إلى بني النضير: أن اثبتوا وتمنعوا، فإنا لن نسلمكم؛ إن قوتلتم قاتلنا معكم، وإن أُخرجتم خرجنا معكم. فتربصوا ذلك من نصرهم فلم يفعلوا، وقذف الله في قلوبهم الرعب.
وسألوا رسول الله ﷺ أن يجليهم ويكف عن دمائهم، على أن لهم ما حملت الإبل من أموالهم إلا الحلقة – السلاح – ففعل. فاحتملوا من أموالهم ما استقلت به الإبل. فكان الرجل منهم يهدم بيته عن نجاف بابه، فيضعه على ظهر بعيره وينطلق به. فخرجوا إلى خيبر، ومنهم من سار إلى الشام.
قال ابن إسحاق: وخلوا الأموال لرسول الله ﷺ، فكانت لرسول الله ﷺ خاصة، يضعها حيث يشاء. قسمها رسول الله ﷺ على المهاجرين الأولين دون الأنصار، إلا سهل بن حنيف وأبا دجانة سماك بن خرشة؛ ذكرا فقرًا، فأعطاهما رسول الله ﷺ. وقال ابن إسحاق: ونزل في بني النضير سورة الحشر بأسرها.
سيرة ابن هشام (٢/١٩٠–١٩٢).

Ibn Isḥāq stated that this occurred after Biʾr Maʿūnah and Uḥud, and after ʿAmr ibn Umayyah returned and killed the two men of Banū ʿĀmir, unaware that they possessed a covenant from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. For this reason, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told him: “You have killed two men whose blood money I must certainly pay.”
Ibn Isḥāq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then went to Banū al-Naḍīr to seek their assistance in paying the blood money for the two slain men of Banū ʿĀmir whom ʿAmr ibn Umayyah had killed, because of the covenant granted to them by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Banū al-Naḍīr and Banū ʿĀmir also had a pact and alliance with one another.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them, they said, “Yes, Abū al-Qāsim, we shall assist you with what you seek.” They then withdrew to confer privately and said, “You will never find this man in a more vulnerable position than he is now”—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting beside the wall of one of their houses—“so who will climb onto this house, cast a rock down upon him, and rid us of him?” ʿAmr ibn Jiḥāsh ibn Kaʿb volunteered, saying, “I will do it.” He climbed up to throw a rock down upon him as they had proposed.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was accompanied by several of his Companions, including Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī. News came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from heaven concerning what the people intended, so he rose and returned to Madinah. When his Companions felt that he had been away for too long, they set out to look for him. They met a man coming from Madinah and asked him about the Prophet ﷺ. He said, “I saw him entering Madinah.” His Companions proceeded until they reached him, and he informed them of the treachery the Jews had intended against him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the Muslims to prepare for war and march against them. Ibn Hishām said: He besieged them for six nights, and the prohibition of wine was revealed.
Ibn Isḥāq said: They fortified themselves against him inside their strongholds. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that some of their palm trees be cut down and burned. They called out to him, “Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption and condemn those who committed it, so why are the palm trees being cut down and burned?”
A group from Banū ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj—including ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, Wadīʿah, Mālik ibn Abī Qawqal, Suwayd, and Dāʿis—had sent word to Banū al-Naḍīr: “Remain steadfast and defend yourselves, for we will never surrender you. If you are fought, we shall fight alongside you, and if you are expelled, we shall leave with you.” Banū al-Naḍīr waited for their promised support, but they did nothing, and Allah cast terror into their hearts.
They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to permit them to depart and spare their lives, on condition that they could take whatever possessions their camels could carry, except weapons. He agreed. They loaded onto their camels whatever property the animals could bear. A man among them would demolish his house to remove the lintel of its door, place it upon his camel, and depart with it. They left for Khaybar, while some traveled to Syria.
Ibn Isḥāq said: They left the property to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It belonged exclusively to him, and he could dispose of it as he wished. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed it among the earliest Emigrants rather than the Anṣār, except for Sahl ibn Ḥunayf and Abū Dujānah Simāk ibn Kharashah, who mentioned their poverty, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them a share. Ibn Isḥāq also said: The whole of Sūrat al-Ḥashr was revealed concerning Banū al-Naḍīr.
The Sīrah of Ibn Hishām (2/190–192).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال ابن إسحاق:
تعبأ رسول الله ﷺ للقتال في سبع مائة رجل، وتعبأت قريش وهم ثلاثة آلاف، ومعهم مائتا فرس قد جنبوها، فجعلوا على ميمنة الخيل خالد بن الوليد، وعلى ميسرتها عكرمة بن أبي جهل.
وأمر رسول الله ﷺ الرماة، وهم خمسون رجلًا: «انضحوا عنا الخيل بالنبل، لا يأتونا من خلفنا، إن كانت لنا أو علينا».
سيرة ابن إسحاق (٥٠٤).

chapters.intro_en_source:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arranged the Muslim army in seven hundred men.
Quraysh formed their army with three thousand men and two hundred horses.
They placed Khālid ibn al-Walīd over the cavalry on the right flank and ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl over the left.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the archers, who numbered fifty men:
“Protect us from the cavalry with your arrows. Do not allow them to reach us from behind, whether victory is ours or against us.”
Sīrat Ibn Isḥāq (504).

بعث رسول الله ﷺ عمر رضي الله عنه في ثلاثين رجلًا إلى عَجُز هوازن بتُرَبَة، فخرج عمر رضي الله عنه ومعه دليل من بني هلال. فكانوا يسيرون الليل ويكمنون النهار.
وأتى الخبر هوازن فهربوا، وجاء عمر محالّهم فلم يلق منهم أحدًا، وانصرف راجعًا إلى المدينة حتى سلك النجدية.
فلما كان بالجَدْر، قال الهلالي لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: هل لك في جمع آخر تركته من خثعم، جاءوا سائرين وقد أجدبت بلادهم؟
فقال عمر: لم يأمرني رسول الله ﷺ بهم؛ إنما أمرني أن أصمد لقتال هوازن بتُرَبَة.
فانصرف عمر راجعًا إلى المدينة.
رواه الواقدي في المغازي (٢/٧٢٢)، عن أسامة بن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبي بكر بن عمر بن عبد الرحمن، قال: بعث رسول الله ﷺ عمر في ثلاثين رجلًا، فذكره.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿUmar رضي الله عنه with thirty men against a remote branch of Hawāzin at Turabah. ʿUmar رضي الله عنه set out with a guide from Banū Hilāl. They travelled by night and concealed themselves during the day.
News of the expedition reached Hawāzin, so they fled. ʿUmar reached their dwellings but found no one there, and he began his return to Madinah by way of the Najd route.
When they reached al-Jadr, the Hilālī guide said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb رضي الله عنه, “Would you like to attack another group from Khathʿam whom I left behind? They have come travelling here because their land has been afflicted by drought.”
ʿUmar replied, “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not command me to attack them. He commanded me only to proceed against Hawāzin at Turabah.”
ʿUmar therefore continued his return to Madinah.
Al-Wāqidī narrated it in al-Maghāzī (2/722), from Usāmah ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿUmar with thirty men,” and then related the report.

كانت في شهر ربيع الآخر سنة ست من مهاجر رسول الله ﷺ. بعث رسول الله ﷺ زيد بن حارثة إلى بني سليم، فسار حتى ورد الجموم، ناحية بطن نخل عن يسارها. وبطن نخل من المدينة على أربعة برد.
فأصابوا عليه امرأة من مزينة يقال لها حليمة، فدلتهم على محلة من محال بني سليم. فأصابوا في تلك المحلة نعمًا وشاءً وأسرى، فكان فيهم زوج حليمة المزنية.
فلما قفل زيد بن حارثة بما أصاب، وهب رسول الله ﷺ للمزنية نفسها وزوجها. «طبقات ابن سعد» (٢/٨٦).

It took place in Rabīʿ al-Ākhir of the sixth year after the Messenger of Allah’s emigration. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Zayd ibn Ḥārithah against Banū Sulaym. He traveled until he reached al-Jumūm, situated to the left of Baṭn Nakhl. Baṭn Nakhl was four postal stages from Madinah.
There they encountered a woman of Muzaynah named Ḥalīmah. She directed them to one of the settlements of Banū Sulaym. At that settlement they captured camels, sheep, and prisoners, among whom was Ḥalīmah’s husband.
When Zayd ibn Ḥārithah returned with the spoils, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted the Muzanī woman her freedom and that of her husband. Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd (2/86).

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال ابن إسحاق: فلما اشتد على الناس البلاء، بعث رسول الله ﷺ – فيما حدثني عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة ومن لا أتهم، عن محمد بن مسلم بن عبيد الله بن شهاب الزهري – إلى عيينة بن حصن بن حذيفة بن بدر، وإلى الحارث بن عوف بن أبي حارثة المري، وهما قائدا غطفان، فأعطاهما ثلث ثمار المدينة على أن يرجعا بمن معهما عنه وعن أصحابه.
فجرى بينه وبينهما الصلح، حتى كتبوا الكتاب، ولم تقع الشهادة ولا عزيمة الصلح، إلا المراوضة في ذلك.
فلما أراد رسول الله ﷺ أن يفعل، بعث إلى سعد بن معاذ وسعد بن عبادة، فذكر ذلك لهما واستشارهما فيه. فقالا له: يا رسول الله، أمرًا تحبه فنصنعه، أم شيئًا أمرك الله به لا بد لنا من العمل به، أم شيئًا تصنعه لنا؟
قال: «بل شيء أصنعه لكم. والله ما أصنع ذلك إلا لأنني رأيت العرب قد رمتكم عن قوس واحدة، وكالبوكم من كل جانب، فأردت أن أكسر عنكم من شوكتهم إلى أمر ما».
فقال له سعد بن معاذ: يا رسول الله، قد كنا نحن وهؤلاء القوم على الشرك بالله وعبادة الأوثان، لا نعبد الله ولا نعرفه، وهم لا يطمعون أن يأكلوا منها تمرة إلا قرًى أو بيعًا. أفحين أكرمنا الله بالإسلام، وهدانا له، وأعزنا بك وبه، نعطيهم أموالنا؟ والله ما لنا بهذا من حاجة. والله لا نعطيهم إلا السيف حتى يحكم الله بيننا وبينهم.
قال رسول الله ﷺ: «فأنت وذاك». فتناول سعد بن معاذ الصحيفة، فمحا ما فيها من الكتاب، ثم قال: ليجهدوا علينا.
سيرة ابن هشام (٢/٢٢٣).

فلما أراد رسول الله ﷺ أن يفعل، بعث إلى سعد بن معاذ وسعد بن عبادة، فذكر ذلك لهما واستشارهما فيه. فقالا له: يا رسول الله، أمرًا تحبه فنصنعه، أم شيئًا أمرك الله به لا بد لنا من العمل به، أم شيئًا تصنعه لنا؟
قال: «بل شيء أصنعه لكم. والله ما أصنع ذلك إلا لأنني رأيت العرب قد رمتكم عن قوس واحدة، وكالبوكم من كل جانب، فأردت أن أكسر عنكم من شوكتهم إلى أمر ما».
فقال له سعد بن معاذ: يا رسول الله، قد كنا نحن وهؤلاء القوم على الشرك بالله وعبادة الأوثان، لا نعبد الله ولا نعرفه، وهم لا يطمعون أن يأكلوا منها تمرة إلا قرًى أو بيعًا. أفحين أكرمنا الله بالإسلام، وهدانا له، وأعزنا بك وبه، نعطيهم أموالنا؟ والله ما لنا بهذا من حاجة. والله لا نعطيهم إلا السيف حتى يحكم الله بيننا وبينهم.
قال رسول الله ﷺ: «فأنت وذاك». فتناول سعد بن معاذ الصحيفة، فمحا ما فيها من الكتاب، ثم قال: ليجهدوا علينا.
سيرة ابن هشام (٢/٢٢٣).
chapters.intro_en_source:
Ibn Isḥāq said: When the hardship became severe for the people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a proposal—as related to me by ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah and other trustworthy narrators from Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbaydullāh ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī—to ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfah ibn Badr and al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf ibn Abī Ḥārithah al-Murrī, the two commanders of Ghaṭafān. He offered them one-third of Madinah’s produce on condition that they withdraw with their forces and leave him and his Companions.
Terms were discussed between him and them, and a document was even written. It was neither witnessed nor finalized as a binding agreement; it remained only a negotiation.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ considered proceeding, he summoned Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, informed them of the proposal, and sought their counsel. They asked: “Messenger of Allah, is this something you desire and want us to carry out, something Allah has commanded and that we must obey, or something you are doing for our sake?”
He replied: “It is something I am doing for your sake. By Allah, I am considering it only because I see that all the Arabs have shot at you from a single bow and have gathered against you from every direction. I wanted to weaken some of their force against you for a time.”
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh said: “Messenger of Allah, both we and these people once followed polytheism and worshipped idols, neither worshipping nor knowing Allah. Even then, they could not hope to eat a single date from us except as hospitality or through purchase. Now that Allah has honored us with Islam, guided us to it, and strengthened us through you and through it, should we give them our property? By Allah, we have no need for this. By Allah, we shall give them nothing but the sword until Allah judges between us and them.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied: “Then it shall be as you say.” Saʿd ibn Muʿādh took the document and erased what had been written in it, then said: “Let them exert all their strength against us.”
The Sīrah of Ibn Hishām (2/223).

chapters.intro_ar_source: قال الله تعالى: (وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ وَٱجْعَل لِّي مِن لَّدُنكَ سُلْطَانًا نَّصِيرًا) [الإسراء: ٨٠]. فأرشده الله وألهمه أن يدعو بهذا الدعاء، أن يجعل له مما هو فيه فرجًا قريبًا، ومخرجًا عاجلًا، فأذن الله تعالى في الهجرة إلى المدينة.

chapters.intro_en_source: Allah Most High said: “And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance and cause me to exit a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority” [al-Isrā’: 80]. Then Allah Most High permitted him to migrate to Medina.

Ibn Isḥāq said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on an expedition in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, intending Quraysh, until he reached Buwāṭ from the direction of Raḍwā. Then he returned to Madinah without encountering any fighting, and he remained there for the rest of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir and part of Jumādā al-Ūlā.
Sīrat Ibn Hishām (1/598).
Buwāṭ, with the bāʾ pronounced either fatḥah or ḍammah, is a mountain of Juhaynah near Yanbuʿ.

قال ابن إسحاق: فلما قدم رسول الله ﷺ لم يقم بها إلا سبع ليال حتى غزا بنفسه يريد بني سليم. وذلك في منتصف محرم، رأس ثلاثة وعشرين شهرًا.
والكدر يقال له: قرقرة الكدر، وقرارة الكدر. جاء في المعالم الأثيرة في السنة والسيرة: “هي بالتحديد إذا صرت من المدينة فكنت بين الصويدرة والحناكية تؤم القصيم، فهي على يمينك في ذلك الفضاء الواسع الذي يمتد إلى معدن بني سليم، مهد الذهب اليوم، غير أن الاسم غير معروف اليوم.” انتهى.
علم النبي ﷺ تجمع سليم وغطفان، فسار إليهم رسول الله ﷺ، وأقام عليه ثلاث ليال، وفر المقاتلون تاركين إبلهم، وعددها خمسمائة، فأخرج خمسها، وقسم أربعة أخماس على المسلمين، فأصاب كل رجل منهم بعيران. وكانوا مائتي رجل.
انظر: طبقات ابن سعد (٢/٣١).

Ibn Isḥāq said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, he stayed there only seven nights before he himself set out intending Banū Sulaym. That was in the middle of Muḥarram, twenty-three months after the Hijrah.
Al-Kudr is also called Qarqarat al-Kudr and Qarārat al-Kudr. It says in al-Maʿālim al-Athīrah fī al-Sunnah wa al-Sīrah: “Its exact location is that when you leave Madinah and are between al-Ṣuwaydirah and al-Ḥanākiyyah, heading toward al-Qaṣīm, it is on your right in that wide open area extending to the mine of Banū Sulaym, today known as Mahd al-Dhahab, although the name is not known today.” End quote.
The Prophet ﷺ learned that Sulaym and Ghaṭafān had gathered, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched toward them and stayed there for three nights. The fighters fled, leaving behind their camels, numbering five hundred. He took out the fifth, and divided the remaining four-fifths among the Muslims, so each man received two camels. They were two hundred men.
See Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd (2/31).

وفي الباب عن الزهري في قوله:
﴿فَمَا أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ وَلَا رِكَابٍ﴾ [الحشر: ٦].
قال: صالح النبي ﷺ أهل فدك وقرى – قد سماها، لا أحفظها – وهو محاصر قومًا آخرين، فأرسلوا إليه بالصلح.
قال:
﴿فَمَا أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ وَلَا رِكَابٍ﴾
يقول: بغير قتال.
قال الزهري: وكانت بنو النضير للنبي ﷺ خالصًا، لم يفتحوها عنوة، افتتحوها على صلح، فقسمها النبي ﷺ بين المهاجرين، ولم يعط الأنصار منها شيئًا إلا رجلين كانت بهما حاجة.
رواه أبو داود (٢٩٧١)، وهو مرسل.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Also relevant to this chapter is the report of al-Zuhrī concerning Allah’s words:
“You spurred neither horses nor riding camels for it.”
 [Al-Ḥashr 59:6]
He said: The Prophet ﷺ concluded peace agreements with the people of Fadak and with certain villages—which the narrator named, though I do not remember their names—while he was besieging another people. They sent to him requesting peace.
He explained the verse:
“You spurred neither horses nor riding camels for it,”
as meaning that it was acquired without fighting.
Al-Zuhrī said: The property of Banū al-Naḍīr belonged exclusively to the Prophet ﷺ. The Muslims did not conquer it by force but acquired it through a peace agreement. The Prophet ﷺ divided it among the Emigrants and gave none of it to the Anṣār except two men who were in need.
Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2971). It is a mursal report.
